latin: Licet natura intellectualis simul omnia intelligat, non tamen hoc est per uirtualem et unitiuam continentiam, sed per mutuam penetrationem formarum, et indissociatam concatenationem totius esse participati, id est, formalis.
translation: Although intellectual nature understands all things at once, this is not through a virtual and unifying containment, but through the mutual interpenetration of forms and the inseparable concatenation of the whole of participated being, that is, formal being.
translation_note: 'unitiuam continentiam' rendered 'unifying containment'; the thesis concerns competing models (unitive-virtual vs. mutual penetration of forms) for how one intellect grasps many things at once.
